- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% relative to model output.
- Underestimate late-period price peaks (especially >85) — adjust upward by 1–3% for values above 82.
- Model tends to lag in correcting downward trends — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast when recent history shows sustained decline.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., >85) — cap forecast at 10% above true peak for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Mean-reversion bias: if 30-day average of true values is 10%+ above forecast, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Forecast tends to overreact to short-term volatility — dampen volatility-adjusted components by 15–20% for high-frequency noise.
